justification: Invariant energy on the frozen state requires objective deformation coordinates.
Differentiation of energy defines stress and tangent.
The reference stationary point is tested by its Hessian.
A tangent requires a twice differentiable interior energy.
Energy plus a unique stable minimum yields conservative recovery.
Recovery needs the reference to be the selected minimum.
Positive tangent supplies a positive acoustic tensor.
Spatial coupling is needed to transport a disturbance.
Reference positivity does not imply stability everywhere.
A smooth approached barrier hardens asymptotically along paths transverse to that barrier, not necessarily along every path.
Finite-boundary blow-up replaces, rather than implies, coercivity on an unbounded domain.
A nonzero gradient Euler-Lagrange term communicates spatially.
Damping can coexist with equilibrium recovery but does not generate its conservative endpoint.
Independent state enlargements violate the frozen native-variable closure.
Zero shear Hessian contradicts positive stiffness on required shear modes.
